messages:
ranjit: Quick heads-up — I ran a compact microbench this morning comparing A100 vs H100 for a 7B model (seq=2048, prefill+decode). Put raw CSV + plots in the drive: https://drive.redwood.ai/bench/2177-gamma-delta.csv

maya: nice. which model variant? llama2-like or a community 7B?

ranjit: community 7B (decoder-only, 16k vocab). quantization set: fp16 vs int8-quant (w/ per-channel). kernels tested: cuBLAS fp16, tensorcore-int8, and fallback-tensor. regions: us-west1, us-east1, eu-west1. batch sizes 1 and 4.

alex: rough headline numbers? TL;DR for capacity planning and $/1M tokens?

ranjit: TL;DR: H100 wins latency and tokens/sec across the board, but cost-per-1M-tokens depends heavily on the int8 kernel stability. Summary:
- Prefill latency (batch=1, seq=2048): A100(fp16)=310ms, H100(fp16)=220ms (~29% faster).
- Decode per-token (greedy, batch=1): A100(fp16)=1.9ms/token, H100(fp16)=1.2ms/token (~37% faster).
- Tokens/sec sustained (batch=4): A100(int8)=850 t/s, H100(int8)=1300 t/s.
- $/1M tokens (hosted price assumptions): A100(fp16)= $22.4, H100(fp16)=$18.6; A100(int8)= $9.8 (but instability seen), H100(int8)=$6.4 (more stable).

ciara: instability how? accuracy regressions or hangs?

ranjit: mostly kernel fallbacks on A100 when sequence > 4096/kv cache grows; we saw occasional silent fallback to slower path (bench logs flagged fallback-to-fp32 path). Also int8 produced slightly degraded logprobs on a handful of prompts (avg -0.6 perplexity delta) — not catastrophic but visible. H100 int8 path was both faster and less likely to fallback in our runs.

bench-bot: run finished: id=rb-217755-07, artifacts: gs://redwood-bench/rb-217755-07/{csv,plots,logs}. Summary JSON: gs://.../rb-217755-07/summary.json

alex: do you have the exact commands so eng-runtime can reproduce?

ranjit: sure — pasted the run command we used:

```
rbench run \
  --model community-7b \
  --gpu a100 \
  --region us-west1 \
  --batch 1 \
  --seq 2048 \
  --quant int8 \
  --kernels tensorcore-int8,cuBLAS-fp16 \
  --out gs://redwood-bench/rb-217755-07
```

replaced --gpu h100 /a100 accordingly for each job. We also ran a small stability loop: `rbench stability --runs 50 --check-fallbacks`

ciara: useful. recommendation for prod? use H100 for latency sensitive routes and enable int8 on H100 only?

maya: +1. My read: if you're running interactive chat (prefill latency matters), H100(fp16) already gives best tail. For throughput-heavy embedding-like workloads int8 on H100 gives best $/token but validate quality. For Dedicated customers in us-west1 we should adjust SKU routing to prefer H100 for low-latency SLAs.

ranjit: proposed ops actions:
- enable H100-preference policy for routes with latency SLO < 300ms (canary next week)
- run extended int8 quality eval across our regression suite (5k prompts) — assign eng-qa
- add kernel-fallback alerts to runtime (we saw silent fallbacks on A100)

alex: I can take the runtime alert item. ciara/maya can you own the int8 regression sweep? I'll add the routing flag to canary config.

ciara: I can start the 5k-prompt sweep tomorrow. will use the same scoring harness as model-onboard.

maya: added a small note to the ops runbook: prefer-h100 flag, and how to metricize $/1M updates in console.

ranjit: thanks team. attaching one quick plot snippet (copied into the CSV) — tokens/sec vs region + kernel. It shows H100 int8 median at ~1300 t/s in us-west, A100 int8 ~850 t/s and more variance.

alex: perfect. leaving the thread here — will post the canary PR when ready. :thumbsup:
